claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 3 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 3 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few questions:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not actually sure about that - my living situation is a bit complicated right now and I'm not certain whether I count as living in the UK or not. Can you still help me figure out if I'd be eligible?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, I can still help you! Since your living situation is uncertain and you're not sure whether you count as living in the UK, let me continue gathering information to get a fuller picture.

**Are you responsible for Alex? That is, do you either:**
- **live with Alex, or**
- **pay at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent in kind) towards looking after Alex - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me - we live together.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that Alex lives with you.

Let me ask another important question:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation, or have they gone to live with someone else?**

conversation.text: No, none of that - Alex is just at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you.

Now, to better understand your situation:

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's part of what makes it complicated, yes. I'm really not sure about my status or where I officially count as living. Is there any way to work out if I might be eligible without sorting all that out first?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand this is complicated for you. Let me ask a few more questions to see if there are any other factors that might affect eligibility:

**Does anyone else currently claim Child Benefit for Alex, or is anyone else also responsible for Alex's care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, and no one else is responsible for their care - it's just me looking after them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:

Let me ask one more question to make sure I have a complete picture:

**Is Alex in any approved education or training, or receiving any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit)? Or, given that Alex is only 3 years old, I assume this doesn't apply?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is only 3, so none of that applies - they're not in any education or training, and they don't get any benefits themselves.
